title: Tracekit event v2
description: One event in a format v2 record log. Additive over tracekit.event.v1: new optional fields and types, and bounds on every string and array. Validated with full-match ASCII patterns.

seq.description: Signer's monotonic counter. Assigned by tracekitd, never by the client.

prev_hash.description: Hash of the previous record in this log; sha256: and 64 zeros for seq 0.

ts_signed.description: Time the signer accepted the event.

agent_id.description: "main" for the top-level agent, otherwise the harness's sub-agent id.

parent_id.description: agent_id of the spawning agent, or null.

source.description: Capture path. transcript = harness-reported, lower trust; import = received over OTLP, or another system's decision (decision_import) (tier T3): receipt only; gateway = model.exchange recorded by the LLM gateway, or a tool call (policy.decision, approval.request, tool.result) or an input (input.observed) the MCP gateway or a tool executor decided, ran or received for its client (tier T2).

transcript.description: C2: what the hook read of the harness transcript at this point (prefix hash). Lets the signer detect later edits, truncation or deletion.

prefix_length.description: Length the signer last acknowledged for this path.

prefix_hash.description: Hash of the first prefix_length bytes as read now.

log_id.description: The record log this event belongs to.

span_id.description: source import: the OpenTelemetry span the record was imported from

ext.description: Non-critical fields (format 1.4), on any record: {name: any strict JSON value}. A verifier that does not interpret a name still checks the record's signature, chain and inclusion, and says it did not interpret the name (docs/format-v2.md section 9).

commitment.description: HMAC-SHA256 of a sha256: digest of agent content under a per-record salt the signer keeps and can reveal for that one record (tracekit signer reveal)

redaction.description: what the signer redacted from this record's content before committing to it; never the values

client_claimed.description: the client said it redacted the content already

client.description: the client's own manifest, as it claimed it

client_redaction_incomplete.description: the client claimed redaction and the signer still found a secret

content.description: Either the (redacted) value or a reference to it. Which one is decided by docs/privacy.md, never by the caller.

os_user_attested.description: true when tracekitd set os_user from the socket peer's credentials rather than trusting the client.

harness.description: 0.3: set only by the signer. The registered harness instance the run.start came from (pid + kernel start time), found from the kernel's view of the sender's process tree.

salt_id.description: the signer's salt id for this record's commitments (salt label <type>:<salt_id>)

policy_hash.description: hash of the policy that produced this decision

tool.description: tool name the decision is for

args_commitment.description: HMAC of the signer's args digest under a per-decision salt the signer can reveal to an auditor; absent when the args failed strict parsing

nondeterministic.description: a fallback-engine match ran out of time and denied

provenance.description: argument values that only untrusted content brought into the run: the top-level argument, the kind of value and the record that brought it; never the value

provenance_state.description: the run's provenance index: complete, partial (an untrusted tool's result came as a digest), truncated (more values than it reads), unavailable (lost in a signer restart) or timeout (this call's values took past the decision's deadline); when not complete, from: untrusted rules match whenever their pattern does

detect.description: format 1.2: what the policy's sequences and limits saw of this call (signer/detect.py): the step each sequence it advanced reached, the count (a sum limit: the total of the call's currency) and window start of each limit it counted, and whether the detector's state is complete or was lost in a restart (unavailable)

rule_ids.description: the rule ids of both class readings, when the client's class hint disagreed and they differ from rule_ids

sums.description: per sum limit: [amount in minor units, currency] of this call

via.description: format 1.2: the gateway or tool executor (its identity, scheme:subject) that wrote this record for the run's client (source gateway, tier T2); the signer takes the call's later steps from it only

caller.description: format 1.2, with via: the client (scheme:subject) the gateway or tool executor decided the call for

incident_id.description: format 1.2: the incident whose hold (ask, TK-HOLD) or quarantine (deny, TK-QUARANTINE) decided the call

same_user.description: true when the approver is the agent's own OS user (dev mode only; not trustworthy)

self_approved.description: the approver is the requester (dev mode only); caps assurance at dev

person.description: an OIDC identity's stable person id

approver_identity.description: the approver as the signer's transport established it

break_glass.description: answered under the break-glass role, which may answer any approval

person.description: an OIDC identity's stable person id

via.description: the bridge (Slack, or the viewer's approval pages) that answered for the approver, as the signer's transport established it

groups.description: user groups the bridge found the approver in

person.description: the person id the signer's config maps the approver to

passkey.description: the WebAuthn credential whose assertion over the approval's binding digest the signer verified

approver_kind.description: format 1.2: an agent approver (approvals.agents) answered; absent for people

asserted.description: format 1.2: what the agent approver says it runs; its own word, never checked

spent.description: format 1.2: rule id -> the argument value this agent approval takes from the rule's sum budget

not_before.description: format 1.2: an agent's approval is consumed from then on (after the rule's veto_s), so people may revoke it first

consume_by.description: format 1.2: an agent's approval is consumed before then (approvals.agent_consume_s), or never

incident_id.description: format 1.2: the answer to a call held by this incident, by the person `person`

salt_id.description: the signer's salt id for this record's commitments (salt label <type>:<salt_id>)

via.description: format 1.2: the gateway or tool executor (its identity, scheme:subject) that wrote this record for the run's client (source gateway, tier T2); the signer takes the call's later steps from it only

cites.description: A signed finding (format 1.4; review_finding), in a findings run: the records of the analysed run it rests on, by run_seq and record hash. A review without cites (a migrated v1 judge verdict) is imported, not checked.

run_id.description: format 1.2: the other run the gap is about (late_activity: the final run that was written to; concurrent_run: the open run this one overlaps; client_counter_gap in a tenant's signer run: the final run whose stream it is; effect_outside_run: the run the client named, its token valid or not, or the effect was attributed to)

sensor.description: format 1.4: the sensor (a kernel sensor, or OpenShell) whose import an observer_lost gap is about

model_message.description: Self-reported model output read from the harness transcript. Opt-in, off by default, lower trust.

model_exchange.description: C3: one model API request/response recorded by the proxy (source=proxy) before the request was forwarded and when the response completed.

salt_id.description: the signer's salt id for this record's commitments (salt label <type>:<salt_id>); absent on records written before salt_id existed

args_unparseable.description: the raw arguments string failed strict parsing

id_synthetic.description: the provider gave no id; the reporting client made this one

said_only.description: format 1.4: a response recorded with what the model said and without the calls it asked for (a harness whose hooks name no call); reconciliation reads no call from it

tool_results_sent.description: tool_use ids whose results the harness sent back in this request

usage.description: Token usage on the response (optional). input_tokens excludes cache reads; reasoning_tokens is part of output_tokens.

person.description: an OIDC identity's stable person id

signer_isolation.description: measured by the signer from the caller's identity, never taken from the client

harness.description: the registered harness process the caller descends from, found by the signer through the harness helper

fail_modes.description: tool class -> fail mode, from the signer's config, never from the client

analyzes.description: a findings run: the run_id of the run of the same tenant it analyses

replay_of.description: a tracekit why replay run: the run_id of the run of the same tenant it replays

investigation.description: with replay_of: the investigation the replay run is an arm of

parent_run.description: format 1.2: the run of the same tenant that started this one, whose run token the caller presented

session.description: with parent_run: the root run of the chain of parents (a run without parent_run is its own session)

fidelity.description: an imported run (source import): what its records say about the calls beyond their receipt

posture.description: format 1.2: the deployment's posture as the operator asserts it in signer.yaml: whether the agent's network is enforced through the egress proxy, whether it acts only through the executor and the MCP gateway, and whether the LLM gateway is its only way to its model (gateway_mandatory); never attested

run_child.description: format 1.2: a run bound to the same harness process registered with this run as its parent_run (signer-written)

provider_executed.description: format 1.2: tool uses the model's provider ran itself (executed_by provider), which no decide covers

coverage.description: the capture layers that reported for the run and the tool calls the signer reconciled

unreconciled.description: reconcile.* records of the run, by kind

paired_by_args.description: format 1.2: calls reconciled by pairing a decide with the model's tool use of the same turn by their arguments, the adapter having had no tool-call id

matrix.description: format 1.2: per action class, how the run was covered: enforced (custody: the only way to act records it), observed (an observer outside the agent saw it and it was reconciled), reported (only the agent's own process reported it) or none; and the layers behind it

salt_id.description: the signer's salt id for this record's commitments (salt label <type>:<salt_id>); absent on records written before salt_id existed

requester_person.description: the requester's stable person id, when an OIDC identity

binding.description: what the approval is bound to; binding_digest is sha256(JCS(binding)), the args bound through args_commitment

executor.description: t2: approval_consume returns the approved arguments and its caller runs exactly those

agent.description: format 1.2: whether an agent approver may answer this approval, computed by the signer from the call's arguments and the run

rules.description: the rules it asked by with approval.agent

conditions_hash.description: sha256 of JCS of those rules' approval.agent sections

args_key.description: an HMAC of the call's arguments under a key of this run: the same in this run for the same arguments, so a call an agent said no to is a person's to answer when asked again

via.description: format 1.2: the gateway or tool executor (its identity, scheme:subject) that wrote this record for the run's client (source gateway, tier T2); the signer takes the call's later steps from it only

incident_id.description: format 1.2: the call is held by this incident: only a person who is not the run's owner, principal or requester answers it

passkey.description: the approval needs a passkey (approval: {passkey: required})

reason.description: format 1.2, on approvals an agent may answer: approvals.ttl_s passed, the run ended, or an agent's approval was not consumed within approvals.agent_consume_s; on any approval: its run was held or quarantined (hold, quarantine)

salt_id.description: the signer's salt id for this record's commitments (salt label <type>:<salt_id>); absent on records written before salt_id existed

decision_id.description: the decision the approval was for (without salt_id: the decision whose salt both commitments are under)

approval_abandoned.description: the adapter will never resume the paused call; the approval ends at once

person.description: an OIDC identity's stable person id

approver_identity.description: the approver as the signer's transport established it

approval_escalated.description: format 1.2: only people answer this approval from now on: an agent approver handed it over, or the signer did (no agent answered within agent_timeout_s, a budget ran out)

approval_revoked.description: format 1.2: a person (or the kill switch, by signer) vetoed an agent's approval before it was consumed

person.description: an OIDC identity's stable person id

approver_identity.description: the approver as the signer's transport established it

asserted.description: format 1.2: what the agent approver says it runs; its own word, never checked

approval_suggested.description: format 1.2: a shadow-mode agent approver's answer, recorded only: it changes nothing

approval_agents.description: format 1.2: the operator's kill switch for agent approvals (in the signer run); switching off revokes every agent approval not consumed yet

input_observed.description: content that entered the run other than as a tool result (observe RPC), indexed for provenance; the value itself is only committed to

source.description: the caller's name for where the content came from

trust.description: the caller's claim; it only decides how this content's own values count

salt_id.description: the signer's salt id for this record's commitments (salt label <type>:<salt_id>)

via.description: format 1.2: the gateway or tool executor (its identity, scheme:subject) that wrote this record for the run's client (source gateway, tier T2); the signer takes the call's later steps from it only

salt_id.description: the signer's salt id for this record's commitments (salt label <type>:<salt_id>); absent on records written before salt_id existed

cert.description: the key's issuance entry from a record-key issuer (tracekit.format.cert, docs/issuer.md)

bridge.description: the v1 ledger this log continues: its key, the seq and hash of its last (key retirement) record

policy_external.description: Another system's decision about a tool call, imported by an identity authorized for decision_import (tier T3). The signer's own policy.decision stays authoritative.

signature.description: verified: the system's Ed25519 signature over its record holds under the key the signer's config pins for it

record.description: the system's own record: an HMAC of its sha256 under this record's salt (salt_id), and its size in bytes

salt_id.description: the signer's salt id for this record's commitments (salt label <type>:<salt_id>)

content_accessed.description: The signer returned retained content of records of a run of this tenant (format 1.1; content_get): who asked, the run, its run_seqs and why. Never the content.

content_erased.description: The signer deleted the retained content of a run of this tenant (format 1.1; content_erase or retention); the run's records are unchanged.

why_finding.description: A finished tracekit why test (format 1.1; why_finding), written in a findings run about the run it analyses: how often the target happened in the control arm (p_with) and with the intervention (p_without) over n paired replays, the interval and verdict with what they were decided on (looks: the sequential test's planned looks, family: the tests corrected for together, min_effect, applied: whether the intervention matched anything, stopped: why the test ended), every replay run with its arm and outcome, and the replay runs of the investigation it does not count (uncounted: the surrogate's ranking calls, arms a budget stop abandoned). rung 1: one recorded model call re-sent; rung 2: the agent loop re-simulated from the recorded run.

incident_opened.description: format 1.2: a trigger of the policy's detection fired (a sequence completed, a limit was exceeded, or a respond trigger), an operator held or quarantined a run (trigger operator), or the detector could not vouch for a decision under an enforced response (detector_unavailable); one open incident per scope, trigger and rule, later matches are incident.updated. mode shadow: no action taken, `would` the configured one; mode enforce: `actions` the ones taken (none while the response engine is paused: then `would` and `reason` say so)

cites.description: the records that make up the match

reason.description: why the actions differ from the configured one (paused, no person approvers), or an operator's reason

in_flight.description: format 1.2: calls allowed (or approved and consumed) and not completed when the response took effect: they may complete after it

incident_updated.description: format 1.2: another match of an open incident (at most one per window of its trigger), written in the run whose record matched

incident_capped.description: format 1.2: a cap on opened incidents was reached: the run's per trigger (cap run), or per minute the tenant's or one run's share of it (cap tenant); the incidents after it are not written

trigger.description: the trigger of the first incident not written

run_held.description: format 1.2: the run is held: every further call is asked of a person (TK-HOLD) and its live approvals expired; written in each run the incident's scope reaches

in_flight.description: format 1.2: calls allowed (or approved and consumed) and not completed when the response took effect: they may complete after it

inherited.description: a new run of a held owner and principal (or of a held parent run) took the hold over

inherit_until.description: until when new runs of this run's owner and attested principal inherit the hold

run_resumed.description: format 1.2: a person ended the hold of one incident on the run (run_resume, which ends each, or incident_resolve of that incident); held_by: the incidents that still hold it

run_quarantined.description: format 1.2: the run is quarantined for good: decisions are deny (TK-QUARANTINE), approvals are refused, a gateway forwards no more model requests

in_flight.description: format 1.2: calls allowed (or approved and consumed) and not completed when the response took effect: they may complete after it

inherit_until.description: until when new runs of this run's owner and attested principal inherit the hold

incident_resolved.description: format 1.2: a person resolved the incident (in the tenant's signer run): its held runs resume, quarantines stay

incident_response.description: format 1.2: an operator paused (enabled false) or resumed the tenant's response engine; detection keeps recording

identity_suspension.description: format 1.2: an identity of the tenant is suspended by an operator (written by the signer that changed the shared list), enforced (each signer that starts enforcing an entry) or lifted

effect_observed.description: format 1.2: network traffic an egress observer outside the agent saw for the run (tracekit.egress), aggregated per host, port and minute; signer-written

attribution.description: token: the client presented the run's token; identity: the observer authenticated the run's owner and the signer picked that owner's latest open run

explained_by.description: what explains the host: a recorded http or model call to it, or the policy's explains; absent: unexplained (a reconcile.unexplained_effect follows)

sensor_effect.description: format 1.4: what a kernel sensor (Tetragon, Falco) reported a process of the run did, or what OpenShell reported of its sandbox (its connections allowed and blocked, its entrypoint's start), imported under the import's own signer identity (an observer's assertion); signer-written

kind.description: exec: the process started; exit: it ended; connect: it connected to host:port; file: the sensor's policy selected a file event of it (a write outside the workspace, in the shipped samples)

exec_id.description: the sensor's id of the process (Tetragon's exec_id)

parent_exec_id.description: exec: the sensor's id of the process that started this one (Tetragon's parent_exec_id)

args_commitment.description: commitment to sha256 of the arguments string as the sensor reported it

salt_id.description: the signer's salt id for this record's commitments (salt label <type>:<salt_id>)

tool_call_id.description: the tool call id the process's environment carried (CODEX_TOOL_CALL_ID): the agent's claim, recorded as it came and checked by no signer (TK-X206 checks it)

denied.description: the sensor (OpenShell's network policy) blocked it

attribution.description: identity: the import mapped the process to the run's owner and the signer picked that owner's latest open run

reconcile_effect.description: format 1.2: a host an observer saw the run reach that no record of the run explains

asserted.description: the status rests on the operator's posture (signer.yaml), not on anything the signer measured

constraint_added.description: format 1.4: a live constraint of the run (constraint_add): what the person's request said not to do in the rest of it, as its client reported it (the Claude Code hook, at UserPromptSubmit). From then on the signer raises a call that breaks it to an ask (rule TK-CONSTRAINT) and never lowers a decision, so a made-up constraint can only hold more calls

kind.description: keep_away: writes of the file; only_change: writes of any other file; read_only: any write; no_push: a git push; no_network: a call that reaches the network

object_commitment.description: keep_away and only_change: commitment to sha256 of the file's lower-cased basename; never the name

salt_id.description: the signer's salt id for this record's commitment (salt label <type>:<salt_id>)

ext_name.description: The name of a non-critical field or record (format 1.4).

ext.description: A non-critical record (format 1.4): its name and any other strict JSON fields, checked as the ext field is.
